title: The Tax Statement
intro: It is tax season. An email says your Zelvora crypto tax statement is ready.
It even has an attachment. Last year Zelvora did send one.
Sniff carefully, this one looks real.

p: If the file does not open,

screen.context: You do have a Zelvora account, and you traded last year.

file.label: Double file ending
file.lens: "pdf.html" is a web page pretending to be a PDF.
file.why: A statement is a plain PDF. A fake ending opens a fake login page when you open it.

addr.label: Look-alike address
addr.why: A different ending is a different owner.

link.label: "Confirm your wallet"
link.lens: The link asks you to sign in or connect your wallet.
link.why: Real statements are downloaded inside the app. Connecting a wallet can hand over your coins.

late.label: Threat of being reported
late.lens: It hints at trouble with the tax office.
late.why: Fake pressure. Real statements do not threaten you.

name.label: Uses your first name
name.why: A name proves little. Scammers know many names.

sender.label: Sender name
sender.lens: Zelvora Tax is a believable team name.
sender.why: Anyone can type any display name.

subject.label: Believable subject
subject.lens: A tax statement in tax season.
subject.why: It fits the time of year, which is the trick.

actions.label: Download my statement inside the Zelvora app
Report it as phishing and delete it

trap.title: Zelvora Reports · Statement
trap.ask: Connect your wallet or sign in to view your statement.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. The fake domain was taken down before it reached more inboxes.

verify.line: The app had your real statement as a plain PDF. The email was fake. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You ignored it safely. Reporting would protect the next person.

go_ahead.line: The "PDF" opened a fake login page. It copied your password and drained the account.

what_if.go_ahead: Opening the app yourself would have shown a real PDF with no login needed.
what_if.verify: Checking in the app was smart. Reporting helps get the fake domain closed.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring it was safe. A quick report protects others.

golden_rule: Never open an attachment you did not expect, and download statements only inside your own app.

quick_check.q: An email says your tax statement is attached as "statement.pdf.html" and asks you to confirm your wallet. What do you do?

options.text: Open it, it is tax season
Do not open it. Download the statement inside the app and report the email
Open it on a second device
Confirm the wallet but skip the file

quick_check.explain: A double ending and a request to connect your wallet are the signs. The app is the safe place.

hints.nudge: Read the file name to the very end.

rows.v: Opens a copy of the login page
In the app, as a plain PDF
